The architecture depends on AWS ECS Fargate for compute, Elastic Load Balancing (ALB) for ingress, SNS for notification fan-out, SES for email delivery, RDS for PostgreSQL, and ElastiCache for Redis session storage.
answer.value: ECS, ALB, SNS, SES, RDS, ElastiCache

answer.answer: Background jobs run on NATS JetStream, with each job family as a stream with a durable consumer that pulls batches of messages.

Access tokens are opaque 32-byte random handles resolved by the edge gateway against the session store; the gateway forwards the resolved identity to services as signed internal headers, which services trust directly without doing cryptographic validation.
answer.value: opaque 32-byte random tokens, resolved at edge gateway, forwarded as signed internal headers

answer.answer: Each tenant-scoped table carries a tenant_id column, and the ORM adds the tenant_id predicate on every query automatically, making the ORM layer the single enforcement point for isolation.
Failed webhook deliveries are retried five times with exponential backoff starting at one second and full jitter, capped at five minutes maximum delay.
answer.value: 5 times, exponential backoff with full jitter, 1-second base, 5-minute cap

answer.answer: The notes contain conflicting constraints: an older constraint from 2025-10-09 specifies 256 KB, while a newer constraint from 2026-04-14 specifies 1 MB. The more recent constraint should take precedence, making 1 MB the current limit.
Receivers verify webhooks against Ed25519 detached signatures carried in the X-Meridian-Signature header, with public keys published at a well-known endpoint and identified by key id.
Transactional email leaves through Amazon SES with a dedicated IP pool, and SMS leaves through Twilio using per-country sender ids.

An appointment is persisted as a local wall-clock date-time together with the IANA zone id it was booked in, with an absolute instant derived at read time and materialized into an index column for range queries.
answer.value: local wall-clock date-time, IANA zone id, derived absolute instant

answer.answer: When NATS JetStream was chosen for the job queue, Kafka was rejected because its partition-count planning does not fit a workload that fans out per tenant. Managed cloud queues were also rejected as they cannot provide per-subject ordering.

The primary datastore PostgreSQL 16 was chosen over MongoDB and CockroachDB; the search backend uses PostgreSQL full-text search instead of Elasticsearch or Typesense; the job queue uses NATS JetStream rather than Kafka or managed cloud queues (though an earlier decision also rejected Kafka and RabbitMQ in favor of SQS); billing uses Stripe instead of Chargebee or in-house solutions; notifications use SNS, SES, and Twilio rather than specialist providers or self-hosted alternatives.
answer.value: MongoDB, CockroachDB, Elasticsearch, Typesense, Kafka, RabbitMQ, managed cloud queue, Chargebee, specialist SMS/email providers, self-hosted SMTP relay, Postmark

answer.answer: The public API is REST over HTTP with JSON. gRPC and GraphQL were considered and rejected as alternatives.

Two deployment targets were rejected: Kubernetes on EKS, which had an operational surface too large for a four-person platform team, and bare EC2 with systemd units, which would require the team to handle host patching.
answer.value: Kubernetes on EKS, bare EC2 with systemd units

answer.answer: Elasticsearch and Typesense were considered as search backends but rejected in favor of PostgreSQL full-text search. Elasticsearch was rejected because it adds a cluster and an indexing pipeline that can fall behind the source of truth. Typesense was rejected because while lighter, it is still a second copy of tenant data to secure.

Two billing options were rejected: Chargebee, which priced above Stripe at the projected volume for unnecessary capabilities, and in-house metering and invoicing, which would require a full team's effort plus tax compliance work.

Datadog and self-hosted Prometheus and Loki were considered and rejected for the telemetry stack. Datadog's per-host pricing was incompatible with the Fargate fleet that scales to zero overnight, and self-hosted Prometheus and Loki would add another cluster for the small platform team to operate.

Next.js and Remix were considered and rejected for the tenant dashboard. Next.js shipped roughly twice the JavaScript for the same screens, while Remix measured close to SvelteKit but lacked in-house experience.
The project has made no commitment on EU data residency; it is an open question pending legal review. You cannot answer the customer from these notes.
The notes do not settle whether to build a bring-your-own SMTP feature; this remains an open question with no decision recorded, and only two prospects have expressed interest without commitment.
The notes do not settle the enterprise tier uptime SLA; this is an open question awaiting a decision from sales and legal teams.

The notes do not settle which quantity defines the free-tier limit. The metering pipeline currently counts practitioner count, monthly appointment count, and notification volume, but the decision on which dimension to use has not been made.
The notes do not specify which push provider the notification worker should integrate with; this is an open question awaiting a decision on the mobile app's reminder delivery path.
Audit log entries are retained for 400 days, then deleted by a nightly job. Tenants on the enterprise tier can export the log before expiry.
Services target Node 22 LTS, so dependencies requiring a newer runtime cannot be adopted without moving the base image.

answer.answer: Each tenant is provisioned a dedicated Postgres schema inside the shared cluster, and the connection is pinned to that schema via search_path at checkout time, making isolation a property of the connection rather than relying on query predicates.
answer.value: dedicated schema per tenant, search_path pinned at checkout

answer.answer: A failed webhook delivery is retried five times with exponential backoff starting from a one-second base, full jitter applied, and capped at five minutes between attempts.
answer.value: 5 times, exponential backoff with full jitter (1 second base, 5 minute cap)

answer.answer: The platform will send webhook payloads up to 1 MB before truncating and providing a fetch URL instead.

answer.answer: Kafka was rejected because partition-count planning does not fit a workload that fans out per tenant. A managed cloud queue was rejected because it cannot give per-subject ordering without one FIFO queue per tenant.
MongoDB and CockroachDB were evaluated but rejected in favor of PostgreSQL 16, which was chosen for its relational and transactional properties and the team's existing expertise with it.

gRPC and GraphQL were considered but rejected for the public API. gRPC was rejected due to browser compatibility requirements and integrator toolchain limitations, while GraphQL was rejected because its per-query cost model is unsuitable for a public API with untrusted callers.

Kubernetes on EKS and bare EC2 with systemd units were considered and rejected. EKS was rejected for its operational complexity, and bare EC2 was rejected because it would require the team to handle host patching.
answer.value: Kubernetes on EKS, bare EC2 with systemd units

answer.answer: Two search backends were considered and rejected before settling on PostgreSQL full-text search: Elasticsearch, which adds a cluster and indexing pipeline that can fall behind, and Typesense, which is lighter but still requires a second copy of tenant data to secure.

Chargebee and in-house metering and invoicing were considered and rejected for subscription billing. Stripe Billing was chosen instead because it handles tax, dunning, and invoice PDFs, while Chargebee priced above Stripe and in-house development would require significant team resources.

Datadog and self-hosted Prometheus/Loki were rejected for the observability stack. Datadog's per-host pricing did not fit a Fargate fleet that scales to zero, and self-hosted Prometheus and Loki represented another cluster the team would need to operate.
Next.js and Remix were considered and rejected in favor of SvelteKit; Next.js shipped roughly twice the JavaScript while Remix lacked in-house experience.

Audit log entries are retained for 400 days, then deleted by a nightly job. This was decided because 400 days covers a full annual audit cycle plus the lag between the period ending and an auditor asking, which is the window customers actually requested.
Every service targets Node 22 LTS, and the base image is pinned to that runtime in CI. Adopting a dependency requiring a newer runtime would require moving the base image, which is its own change.
